transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Carter (VP Eng, HarborTrust), Aisha Khan (Cloud Architect, HarborTrust), Leo Martin (InfoSec, HarborTrust)

Summary: quick discovery on private VPC options, network topology, what HarborTrust needs for data residency and compliance, and next steps to run a tech deep dive and provide pricing.

[00:00:05] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, nice to meet you all. real quick we'll run through our private vpc options and then go deep on your networking constraints.
[00:00:18] Tom: hey maya, thanks. i'm tom. short background — we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, leaning private because of compliance and customer data controls.
[00:00:30] Aisha: hi, yeah i'm aisha, cloud architect. we manage our vpcs across us-east-1 and eu-west-1, some latency-sensitive stuff in us-west-2. curious about peering vs private endpoints.
[00:00:41] Leo: leo here, i'll be focused on encryption, audit logs, and key management.
[00:00:45] Ravi: great, i'll cover the network/topology aspects and what our private offering looks like. quick, is anyone on the call using transcoders? sorry, slip — i mean, are you using a central transit VPC or direct peering today?
[00:00:58] Tom: we have a hub-and-spoke with transit gateway in us-east-1, spokes in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for europe. we also have strict CIDR ranges, we try to avoid overlaps.
[00:01:12] Maya: perfect. at a high level, our Private deployment is a customer-managed VPC that connects to a Redwood-managed control plane. we support three main connectivity patterns: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink/private endpoints, and transit gateway integration. each has tradeoffs around routing, cross-account permissions, and egress.
[00:01:35] Aisha: can you run through the pros/cons quickly? particularly for large egress and for cross-region calls.
[00:01:42] Ravi: yeah. peering is simple if CIDRs don't overlap, lower latency, but it's per-VPC and doesn't traverse transit gateway unless you do some more setup. PrivateLink (our private endpoints) gives you an endpoint service we publish into your account — it works across AZs and can be more controlled for IAM and security, but you pay interface endpoint costs and there is some per-connection overhead. transit gateway can centralize routes if you already use it, but you need to be careful about route propagation and ASG... sorry, route tables — my bad.
[00:02:15] Tom: that matches our thinking. we do want to avoid opening public internet egress. How does authentication happen on the private control plane? is the data plane fully in our VPC?
[00:02:26] Maya: good q. control plane communication (management API) hits a Redwood control plane — in private offering we can either expose it over a private endpoint inside your account (PrivateLink) or run a customer-hosted control plane in your VPC (air-gapped option for highly regulated customers). the data plane — inference workers — can be deployed in a dedicated VPC that we either operate in your account or we operate in our private environment with a peered connection; we can support both models depending on your requirement for data residency.
[00:02:55] Leo: if you host the data plane outside our account, what assurances do we have about data at rest encryption and KMS?
[00:03:03] Ravi: we support customer-managed KMS keys for encrypting model artifacts and logs. if you want HSM integrations, we have partners and can support Bring Your Own Key via external HSM for certain private deployments; we'll share the vendor list.
[00:03:16] Aisha: region thing — we need to run inference in eu-west-1 for EU customer data and us-east-1 for US customers; can Redwood place inference workers in both regions under a single private deployment?
[00:03:29] Maya: yes — we can provision regional worker pools and route traffic based on region or latency policies. there are some limitations on cross-region control plane reachability — if you want fully customer-hosted control plane in eu-west-1 we can discuss that. typically we run regional control plane endpoints and replicate configs.
[00:03:47] Tom: what about CIDR overlap? our corporate CIDRs are 10.0.0.0/16 in us-east and 10.1.0.0/16 in us-west. we also have partner networks that occasionally overlap.
[00:03:58] Ravi: overlaps are common pain. options: (1) we can ask you to allocate a non-overlapping CIDR for the Redwood worker VPCs, (2) use PrivateLink which avoids peering routes and thus CIDR constraints, or (3) use NAT/forwarding with proxying but that's more complex. PrivateLink usually is the easiest if you can't change CIDRs.
[00:04:20] Aisha: ok. curious on bandwidth/throughput and egress costs — we have heavy batch workflows.
[00:04:27] Maya: for heavy throughput we recommend Dedicated pools (reserved GPUs) and colocating in the same region as your workload. Dedicated + Private gives you predictable throughput and lower per-token cost. egress depends on where the workers live; if everything is inside your account, egress charges are your cloud provider's usual inter-AZ/inter-region rates. we can also discuss compression and caching to reduce egress.
[00:04:51] Leo: audit logs — we need immutable logs sent to our centralized SIEM, retention 7 years, chain-of-custody. can you push logs to our Kinesis/CloudWatch/S3?
[00:05:02] Ravi: yes, we can stream audit logs to your account S3 or a logging endpoint; we also provide a copy in the Redwood control plane for troubleshooting. we support configurable retention and can sign an addendum for long-term retention if needed.
[00:05:15] Tom: perf test question — can we run an initial benchmark in our VPC?
[00:05:20] Maya: absolutely. typical pilot: we set up a small worker pool in your account or peered VPC, run a set of representative prompt workloads, measure latency and token cost, then optimize batch size/kv cache. Ravi will own the tech deep dive.
[00:05:33] Aisha: what's the onboarding time? we have a compliance deadline end of Q2.
[00:05:38] Maya: onboarding can be as fast as 2–3 weeks for a pilot if we have network approvals and CIDRs; production dependent on procurement and dedicated capacity which can be 6–8 weeks.
[00:05:47] Leo: data residency / model training — we won't allow model fine-tuning with customer PII on shared models. can you guarantee that?
[00:05:55] Ravi: by default we don't expose training/fine-tuning on the hosted shared clusters. for private deployments we can lock down the environment — fine-tuning would be on customer-managed infrastructure with explicit contracts. we'll document the policy in the security pack.
[00:06:10] Tom: network firewall question — can we restrict egress from worker subnets to only our endpoints?
[00:06:15] Ravi: yes, when workers run in your account you control security groups and NACLs. when workers run in a Redwood-managed account behind peering, we enforce strict egress controls and can restrict to specific S3 endpoints and control plane IPs; we can also put NAT gateways in place if you require.
[00:06:30] Aisha: any requirements for route table propagation with transit gateway?
[00:06:34] Ravi: you need to allow specific route associations and not blacklist Redwood's peer attachment. we'll provide a sample Terraform snippet for TGW attachments and route propagation.
[00:06:44] Maya: also want to flag certificate management — for private endpoints we use ACM-managed certs in AWS or customer-provided certs if you prefer.
[00:06:53] Leo: okay on compliance front: do you have SOC 2 and ISO docs we can attach to our vendor review?
[00:06:59] Maya: yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary, plus our incident response and penetration testing reports under NDA.
[00:07:08] Tom: pricing — give us a ballpark for dedicated GPU pools vs running in our account?
[00:07:13] Maya: rough numbers — Dedicated reserved pools are higher upfront but lower per-token; private in your account shifts infra costs to you (EC2/EBS) and we charge a platform fee + per-inference unit. we'll send a preliminary pricing sheet.
[00:07:25] Aisha: are there region constraints for your managed images? eg some AMIs are only in us-east-1 and need replication?
[00:07:33] Ravi: we image and publish worker AMIs in all major regions we support; for Private we can replicate to your account or bring your own AMI. multi-region replication requires an extra step but is standard.
[00:07:45] Tom: support SLAs — what uptime and response times for private deployments?
[00:07:49] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. Private in-customer-account support availability is a bit different — platform maintenance windows are scheduled, and we offer enterprise support add-on for faster response times.
[00:07:59] Leo: one more security nitty-gritty — can you do customer-managed identities for service accounts (IRSA) and map to our IAM roles?
[00:08:08] Ravi: yes, we can integrate with your IAM roles. if you're on EKS we can do IRSA mappings, or for EC2 tasks we can use instance profiles or assume-role flows.
[00:08:19] Aisha: any gotchas with PrivateLink and cross-region?
[00:08:22] Ravi: PrivateLink is regional. for cross-region you'd either set up endpoints in each region or use a regional transit solution. if you need single control plane spanning regions, we replicate endpoints or offer customer-hosted control plane in specific regions.
[00:08:36] Maya: let's talk blockers — from what i heard you need: (1) confirm CIDR overlaps / give us network diagram, (2) review SOC2 and KMS docs, (3) technical deep dive with your network team — does that sound right?
[00:08:47] Tom: yes, exactly. also want to see a sample terraform snippet and a security addendum.
[00:08:52] Maya: we'll include that.
[00:08:55] Ravi: quick note on troubleshooting — we surface per-request traces, token-level cost, and kv-cache hit rates in the console; for private deployments we can push traces to your tracing backend as well.
[00:09:08] Leo: good. what about pen-test windows and vulnerability scanning cadence?
[00:09:12] Maya: yearly pen tests, quarterly vuln scans; we can align to your schedule or accept your attestation if you have a strict vendor program.
[00:09:22] Tom: timeline again — if we start pilot next week how soon can you spin up a worker pool in our account?
[00:09:28] Ravi: assuming network approvals, side accounts and IAM roles provisioned, we can have a small pilot in 10–14 business days.
[00:09:35] Aisha: ok we'll try to get CIDR info and region list to you by Friday.
[00:09:40] Maya: awesome. any final q's?
[00:09:44] Leo: no, just please send the SOC2 and the KMS/HSM vendor list.
[00:09:48] Maya: will do. recap on next steps: maya share docs; ravi schedule deep dive; aisha share cidrs; redwood share pricing and terraform snippets.
[00:09:58] Tom: thanks everyone. good call.
[00:10:02] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with notes and links. bye.

Notes about transcription: some overlaps and names may be slightly mis-attributed; this is machine transcription with manual review.
